businessModel: Free; ads, content feed and traffic into Tencent ecosystem (WeChat, QQ, Tencent Docs, Tencent Cloud AI)
updateCadence: Frequent minor releases per vendor changelog; not independently checked
summary: QQ Browser is Tencent's Chromium-based browser, widely used in China, with document/PDF tools, video features and, since April 2026, the QBotClaw agent that automates tasks and can be driven from WeChat.
bestFor: Users in mainland China wanting Tencent/WeChat integration
People who want built-in document/PDF handling
notFor: Users outside China needing English polish
Anyone who dislikes feeds and ads

pros.title: QBotClaw agent
pros.detail: Natural-language automation (e.g. price comparisons across Taobao and JD) launched April 2026, remote-controllable from WeChat.

pros.title: Tencent ecosystem
pros.detail: Deep integration with WeChat, QQ and Tencent Docs.

pros.title: Built-in tools
pros.detail: Document, PDF, video and screenshot utilities are bundled.

cons.title: Security history
cons.detail: Citizen Lab (2016) found insecure data transmission and unsafe update mechanisms in Windows and Android versions.

cons.title: Ad and feed heavy
cons.detail: Start page feeds and promotions are central to the model.

cons.title: Early agent limits
cons.detail: Hands-on test hit API rate limits and needed manual logins.

cons.title: Opaque versions
cons.detail: Current build and Chromium base not published in an easy-to-verify place.

faq.q: Does QQ Browser have an AI agent?
faq.a: Yes. Tencent Cloud announced QBotClaw on 2026-04-08; Mac was live first and Windows was "coming soon" at launch.
Wikipedia describes Chromium-based engine upgrades since version 9.0 (2015); the current Chromium version is not published in sources found.
Not by default. Citizen Lab reported insecure data handling in 2016, and it is a Tencent ad/content product.
